content.text:
**Navy P-3** usually refers to the **Lockheed P-3 Orion**, especially the **P-3C Orion** used by the U.S. Navy.

**Quick overview:**
- **Type:** Four-engine turboprop maritime patrol aircraft
- **Main missions:** Anti-submarine warfare, maritime surveillance, reconnaissance, anti-surface warfare
- **Introduced:** Early 1960s; P-3C first delivered to the Navy in 1969
- **Sensors:** Sonobuoys, radar, electronic surveillance gear, and a Magnetic Anomaly Detector boom in the tail
- **Weapons:** Torpedoes, depth charges, mines, and anti-ship missiles such as Harpoon
- **Replacement:** The U.S. Navy has largely replaced the P-3C with the **Boeing P-8A Poseidon**, though P-3-based variants like the **EP-3E Aries II** have been used for signals intelligence. ([navy.mil](https://www.navy.mil/Resources/Fact-Files/Display-FactFiles/Article/2166367/p-3c-orion-and-ep-3-aries/no/no/p-3c-orion/?utm_source=openai))

A distinctive feature is the long **MAD boom** extending from the tail, used to help detect submarines by sensing magnetic disturbances.
